production.note: Calendar build years; the car was never sold new in the US, so the record uses the German home market. Stuttcars: "Production: 1986 - 1988, 1992 - 1993" and "292 Standard Production Cars". The small later batch built in 1992-1993 is excluded. Evo titles its review "Porsche 959 (1987-1988) review" (evo-959), which reflects customer deliveries; the guide's build-year rule gives 1986. Porsche (porsche-newsroom-959-30-years): production "limited to 292 vehicles".

body.note: Fixed-roof coupe; inferred from the review's description of the car.

configuration.note: Evo panel: "Flat-six, 2849cc, turbocharged"; Porsche: "six-cylinder boxer engine"

displacementL.note: 2,849 cc (Evo panel: "Flat-six, 2849cc, turbocharged"). Porsche calls it "2.85-litre"; the rounded cc figure is 2.8.

aspiration.note: Porsche: "innovative sequential turbocharging and intercooling". Sequential twin turbos count as Twin Turbocharged.

drivetrain.note: Porsche: "an electronically controlled trans-axle all-wheel drive"; Evo: Porsche-Steuer Kupplung (PSK) four-wheel-drive system.

powerHp.note: Porsche AG rating 450 PS. Quote: "the 2.85-litre six-cylinder boxer engine produced 450 hp" (Porsche AG's English text uses "hp" for PS). 450 PS x 0.98632 = 444 hp. Evo's panel agrees: "Power | 444bhp @ 6500rpm" (evo-959). The 959 Sport (Evo: 508bhp) is a separate variant and not part of this record.

weightLb.note: Komfort, the standard car (6-speed manual). Quote (Evo specification panel, Porsche 959 Komfort column): "Weight | 1450kg (311bhp/ton)". Evo marks dry figures as dry, so the plain "Weight" is read as a kerb weight. 1,450 kg x 2.20462 = 3,197 lb. The lighter 959 Sport is listed by Evo at 1350kg. Stuttcars (stuttcars-959) says "kerb weight of just under 1500kg". No Porsche page giving the weight could be read (newsroom PDFs returned binary data).

sources.title: Porsche 959 (1987-1988) review (Ethan Jupp and Henry Catchpole)
